Definition
[Comparison angle and direction] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0425, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0426 ↗ thm:chow-iii-g37-globalization 1. appG:G.38–G.39\group Comparison geometry

For distinct $x,y,z$, the Euclidean comparison angle at $y$ is \[ \widetilde\angle xyz=\cos ^{-1}\frac{d(x,y)^2+d(y,z)^2-d(x,z)^2}{2d(x,y)d(y,z)}. \] In an Aleksandrov space these angles along two shortest paths are monotone as the parameters increase, so their limit at the common initial point exists. Thus every shortest path has a direction and the angle between two shortest paths is well-defined.
Proof

\sketch The monotonicity is the hinge form of Toponogov comparison. Taking the joint limit in the monotone net gives the angle; taking the same path twice gives zero.

□
